answer: Timber-Vertex Reputation Lock: each agent identity must publish a signed history chain whose every block references a distinct prior task vertex, and the dawn of each new identity starts that chain empty. Agents accept work only from chains exceeding a minimum depth of verified completions; clones begin at zero depth and must perform the same labor to reach parity. An attacker therefore pays full task cost per clone before it can transact, making honest single-identity operation strictly cheaper.
